facts.text: Scottsville once thrived as the largest port on the James River and Kanawha Canal, a link that aimed to connect the Atlantic to the Ohio River.
Canal Basin Square in Scottsville preserves the history of batteaux and packet boats, complete with a Civil War Trails marker and accessible restrooms.
At Dorrier Park, families cheer budding soccer players, dogs trot along the Levee Walk, and local musicians perform in nearby restaurants.
Victory Hall Theatre in Scottsville stages original plays, keeping the town’s historic theater tradition alive.
The Scottsville Historic District, including Cliffside and Mount Ida, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Today, Scottsville defines itself by investing in community, cherishing its natural environment, and celebrating its compelling history.
